name: The Theorist, Jace Beleren
oracle_text:
At the beginning of each opponent's draw step, you draw a card.
+1: Create a 1/1 blue Illusion creature token.
−2: For each opponent, return up to one target artifact or creature that player controls to its owner's hand.
−6: Draw three cards. Then put X +1/+1 counters on each creature you control, where X is the number of cards in your hand.
blocked_sentences: +1: Create a 1/1 blue Illusion creature token.

needs.what: a token id for a plain 1/1 blue Illusion creature token with NO abilities -- e.g. `illusion_1_1_u`: name "Illusion", oracle_text "1/1 blue Illusion creature token.", types ["Creature"], subtypes ["Illusion"], power 1, toughness 1, colors ["U"], color_identity ["U"], no keywords, is_token true. It is the shipped `illusion_1_1_u_flying` entry in data/cards/tokens.cards.json with the keywords list dropped and the id and oracle_text trimmed to match, so it is a one-line data change. The vanilla blue Illusion is the standard token of the Jace/Illusion shell, so the single id closes a family rather than just this card.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: token_ids is a closed list and its only Illusion is `illusion_1_1_u_flying` -- confirmed against data/cards/tokens.cards.json, where that entry carries "keywords": ["flying"]. Size, colour and creature type are all right; the flying is not, and the brief forbids substituting a nearly-right token. Flying is not cosmetic on a card whose ultimate also makes those Illusions large: an evasive army and a ground-stalled one are different cards, and the printed token has no evasion. `create_token` cannot spell the difference from the card either -- op_options gives it only `token`, `amount`, `as`, `attacking`, `controller` and `tapped`, with no keyword, colour, subtype or power/toughness override. Nor can the token be patched after creation: there is no remove-keyword op in `ops` at all (grant_keyword only adds), `lose_all_abilities` is a static_effect that would have to be permanent and would strip anything the token ever gained as well, and `animate` on a create_token `as` binding stores an until-end-of-turn TempEffect, so whatever it set would fall off at cleanup where the printed token is permanently a flightless 1/1. The next-nearest ids are `fish_1_1_u` (right size and colour, wrong creature type, and these tokens are meant to be Illusions) and `hero_1_1_c` (colourless).

notes:
The token is the ONLY blocker. Every other printed line is expressible today and the card ships the moment the one-line token id lands. Written out in full:

Card: id "the_theorist_jace_beleren", name "The Theorist, Jace Beleren", mana_cost "{2}{U}{U}", types ["Planeswalker"], supertypes ["Legendary"], subtypes ["Jace"], colors ["U"], color_identity ["U"], loyalty <see the LOYALTY note at the end>, oracle_text verbatim as above. No `sorcery_speed_only` on any ability -- 606.3 is the loader's job (docs/card-dsl.md, Planeswalkers).

abilities:
1) {"kind": "triggered", "text": "At the beginning of each opponent's draw step, you draw a card.", "trigger": {"event": "draw_step", "controller": "opponent"}, "effects": [{"op": "draw", "player": "you", "amount": {"const": 1}}]}. The controller clause is right rather than guessed: triggers._trigger_actor lists draw_step among the events whose actor is event.player, and turn._draw_step fires DRAW_STEP with player=active_player, so "opponent" reads "whose draw step it is" -- exactly the printed line. Nothing new is needed for it, even though no shipped card writes a draw_step trigger yet.
2) {"kind": "activated", "text": "+1: Create a 1/1 blue Illusion creature token.", "cost": {"loyalty": 1}, "effects": [{"op": "create_token", "token": "<the new illusion_1_1_u id>"}]}. This is the blocked line.
3) {"kind": "activated", "text": "−2: For each opponent, return up to one target artifact or creature that player controls to its owner's hand.", "cost": {"loyalty": -2}, "targets": [{"id": "t1", "kind": "permanent", "count": "any", "one_per_player": true, "selector": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "opponent", "any_types": ["Artifact", "Creature"]}}], "effects": [{"op": "return_to_hand", "objects": {"target": "t1"}}]}. `one_per_player` is the proven shape for "for each player, up to one target ... that player controls": shipped unexplained_absence writes it, docs/card-dsl.md has the section, and loader/targets.py refuses it without count "any". `controller: "opponent"` in the selector is what narrows "each player" to "each opponent". A hand-authored spec per seat is the approximation to refuse.
4) {"kind": "activated", "text": "−6: Draw three cards. Then put X +1/+1 counters on each creature you control, where X is the number of cards in your hand.", "cost": {"loyalty": -6}, "effects": [{"op": "draw", "player": "you", "amount": {"const": 3}}, {"op": "add_counters", "counter": "+1/+1", "amount": {"cards_in_hand": "you"}, "objects": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "count": "all"}}]}. Both halves are shipped shapes: {"cards_in_hand": "you"} is in value_keys and written by cards already in the pool, and the add_counters selector is byte-for-byte celes_rune_knight's and felidar_retreat's. The counters are read after the draw resolves, which is what "Then" means.

Expectation: {"zone": "battlefield", "battlefield_count": 33}. The fallback shape is the correct one here rather than laziness: the harness casts the card and stops, so neither loyalty ability is ever activated (trap 1), and the position is your own turn-1 precombat main, so no opponent's draw step happens and the triggered ability never fires (trap 5). A planeswalker resolving makes 33 permanents -- the 30 lands and 2 creatures already there, plus itself (trap 3).

LOYALTY -- the one datum the answer will still need, which the packet does not carry. `loyalty` is a plain number on the card (docs/card-dsl.md, Planeswalkers) and it is not optional in practice: cards/loader/__init__.py emits the self_enters_with_counters replacement only when model.loyalty is not None, and its own comment says a planeswalker that entered with no loyalty is binned by the zero-loyalty state-based action the instant it resolves -- which would fail the expectation above. Neither the packet, data/catalog/cards.sqlite (whose columns stop at toughness and record no loyalty for any card) nor data/generated/cards/pool.cards.json carries a loyalty for this card, so it has to be read off the printed card before the answer is written. Scryfall id 20bb8c55-4b0b-425f-8201-b54fa2fdde86, set "fra", mythic. This is a catalog/packet data hole rather than a DSL capability, so it is deliberately not filed as a `needs` entry, but the card cannot be finished without it.
